newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas governor, legislature compromise on bill.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas governor, legislature compromise on bill.

text.p: The Arkansas legislature on Wednesday agreed to excise a reference to the state's recent floods and tornadoes as "acts of God," and Gov. Mike Huckabee announced he would promptly sign a pending disaster relief bill.
Huckabee, a Baptist minister, had objected last week to the bill sent for his signature, saying he did not believe such events as tornadoes and floods were "acts of God."
The compromise involved changing 'acts of God" to "natural causes."
"The governor can show everybody how religious he is and the rest of us can help disaster victims," snapped State Representative Pat Flanagin, who sponsored the amendment approved Wednesday.
Twenty-four people were killed and tens of millions of dollars in damage done to property on March 1 when a series of tornadoes raced across Arkansas.

The legislation, which was introduced before the tornadoes occurred, would prevent property insurance companies from cancelling policies due to losses resulting from storms, floods or other natural calamities.

But in a message to the legislature last week, Huckabee asked that the bill be recalled and the term "natural disasters" substituted for "acts of God." Huckabee said he could not, as a matter of conscience, believe that God would will death and destruction in the form of storms.
Huckabee's objections were addressed on Wednesday.

"We'd been supportive of the bill all along," said Rex Nelson, Huckabee's press secretary. "This new language addresses the concerns the governor had and we can quickly get this bill signed into law."
Both Flanagin and Nelson said they knew of no policies that had been cancelled after Huckabee objected to the bill.
